name: Margaret Thatcher
kicker: Britain’s “Iron Lady” · First female UK prime minister, won the Falklands War
briefing: Margaret Thatcher grew up working in her father’s grocery store and trained as a chemist before going into politics. As Britain’s first female prime minister, she took on labor unions, sold off government-owned companies, and led the country to victory in the 1982 Falklands War. Soviet newspapers nicknamed her the “Iron Lady” for her tough stance against communism, and the name stuck for the rest of her career.
answerHtml: Margaret Thatcher (or Margaret Hilda Thatcher or Baroness Thatcher; prompt on “the Iron Lady”)

trap.title: Iron Lady, not the Queen
trap.body: Soviet media gave Thatcher the nickname “Iron Lady” for her tough anti-communist stance — the same kind of tough-leader label sometimes given to other leaders, like India’s Indira Gandhi, so “Iron Lady” alone isn’t enough. Kids also sometimes confuse Thatcher, the elected prime minister who ran the government, with Queen Elizabeth II, the unelected head of state at the same time — two different jobs held by two different women.
trap.fix: If the clue mentions the Falklands War, privatization, the miners’ strike, or “Milk Snatcher,” it’s Thatcher. If it mentions the crown, Buckingham Palace, or decades on the throne, it’s the Queen.
trap.line: Real answer line: Margaret Thatcher (or Margaret Hilda Thatcher; or Baroness Thatcher)
